Lift an idempotent successively modulo m^n by the standard polynomial correction to e^2-e and pass to the complete limit. If e lifts a central idempotent, each finite O-module X=eOH(1-e) or (1-e)OHe satisfies X=mX. For a finite generating tuple, write these relations as (I-A)x=0 with entries of A in m; the adjugate identity gives det(I-A)X=0, while det(I-A) is congruent to 1 modulo m and hence is a unit. Thus X=0 and e is central. This finite determinant argument replaces the published AC-stated Nakayama theorem. Central lifts are unique modulo the radical: if central idempotents e,f have e-f in J, then e(1-f) and f(1-e) are idempotents in J and hence zero. Orthogonal decompositions therefore lift and reduce bijectively, so primitivity is preserved in both directions.
